title: These Tiny VR Goggles Lets Mice See Virtual Reality Worlds #tech #virtualreality #shorts
description:
MouseGoggles: Scientists Build a Tiny VR Headset for Mice

Scientists have developed MouseGoggles, a miniature virtual reality (VR) headset designed specifically for mice. Created by Matthew Isaacson and his team, the open-source system could make VR experiments in neuroscience smaller, simpler and more accessible.

Traditional mouse VR systems often use large screens or LED displays placed around the animal. These setups can be expensive, take up significant space and may be obstructed by cameras or other laboratory equipment.

MouseGoggles solves this problem by placing tiny displays directly in front of the mouse’s eyes. The headset provides independent binocular vision across a field of view of about 140 degrees, creating a more immersive virtual environment.

The system also includes infrared cameras for eye tracking and pupil measurement, allowing researchers to study how the animal's eyes respond during VR experiences.

Tests showed that visual-cortex recordings successfully responded to images presented through the headset. Mice also demonstrated learning during reward-based tasks and defensive responses to virtual objects approaching them.

The compact system can run using a single Raspberry Pi computer and fit within a footprint of about 14 × 14 cm with a linear treadmill.

The researchers believe MouseGoggles could enable new studies of vision, navigation, learning, fear and multisensory behavior in animals.

Read full article here: https://www.uncoverreality.in/2026/09/scientists-build-tiny-vr-headset-that.html

Reference: Isaacson, M., Chang, H., Berkowitz, L. et al. MouseGoggles: an immersive virtual reality headset for mouse neuroscience and behavior. Nat Methods 22, 380–385 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02540-y
